title: Solving Linear Equations
description: Multi-step linear equations with variables on both sides, plus two find-the-mistake problems.

source.name: IM 6–8 Math, Grade 8, Unit 4: Linear Equations and Linear Systems
source.attribution: Adapted from IM 6–8 Math by Open Up Resources and Illustrative Mathematics, CC BY 4.0.
source.changes: Selected practice problems from three lessons, renumbered and laid out as one printable worksheet with answer space. Problem text is unchanged.

problems.text:
Solve each of these equations. Explain or show your reasoning.
\(2(x+5)=3x+1\)
\(3y-4=6-2y\)
\(3(n+2)=9(6-n)\)

Solve each equation, and check your solution.
\(\frac19(2m-16) = \frac13(2m+4)\)
\(-4(r+2)=4(2-2r)\)
\(12(5+2y)=4y-(6-9y)\)
problems.solution: Multiply the first equation by 9: 2m − 16 = 6m + 12, so −28 = 4m and m = −7. −4r − 8 = 8 − 8r, so 4r = 16 and r = 4. 60 + 24y = 4y − 6 + 9y = 13y − 6, so 11y = −66 and y = −6. Checks: m = −7 gives −30/9 = −10/3 on both sides; r = 4 gives −24 on both sides; y = −6 gives −84 on both sides.

problems.text:
Solve each of these equations. Explain or show your reasoning.
\(2b+8-5b+3=-13+8b-5\)
\(2x+7-5x+8=3(5+6x)-12x\)
\(2c-3=2(6-c)+7c\)

Solve each equation and check your solution.
\(-3w-4=w+3\)
\(3(3-3x)=2(x+3)-30\)
\(\frac13(z+4)-6=\frac23(5-z)\)
problems.solution: −3w − 4 = w + 3, so −7 = 4w and w = −7/4. 9 − 9x = 2x + 6 − 30 = 2x − 24, so 33 = 11x and x = 3. Multiply by 3: z + 4 − 18 = 10 − 2z, so 3z = 24 and z = 8. Checks: w = −7/4 gives 5/4 on both sides; x = 3 gives −18 on both sides; z = 8 gives −2 on both sides.

problems.text:
Andre solved an equation, but when he checked his answer he saw his solution was incorrect. He knows he made a mistake, but he can’t find it. Where is Andre’s mistake and what is the solution to the equation?
\(-2(3x-5) = 4(x+3)+8\)
\(-6x+10 = 4x+12+8\)
\(-6x+10 = 4x+20\)
\(10 = -2x+20\)
\(-10 = -2x\)
\(5 = x\)

answer.sample: The mistake is going from −6x + 10 = 4x + 20 to 10 = −2x + 20. Adding 6x to both sides gives 10 = 10x + 20, so −10 = 10x and x = −1.
criteria: Identifies the step from −6x + 10 = 4x + 20 to 10 = −2x + 20 as the mistake (6x was subtracted on the right instead of added)

problems.solution: From −6x + 10 = 4x + 20, add 6x to both sides: 10 = 10x + 20. Then −10 = 10x, so x = −1. Check: −2(−3 − 5) = 16 and 4(2) + 8 = 16.

problems.text:
Clare was solving an equation, but when she checked her answer she saw her solution was incorrect. She knows she made a mistake, but she can’t find it. Where is Clare’s mistake and what is the solution to the equation?
\(12(5+2y) = 4y-(5-9y)\)
\(72+24y = 4y-5-9y\)
\(72+24y = -5y-5\)
\(24y = -5y-77\)
\(29y = -77\)
\(y = \frac{-77}{29}\)

answer.sample: In the second line, 12 · 5 is 60, not 72, and −(5 − 9y) is −5 + 9y, not −5 − 9y. Correctly: 60 + 24y = 13y − 5, so 11y = −65 and y = −65/11.
criteria: Identifies an error in the step from the first line to the second: 12 · 5 = 60, not 72, and/or the sign of 9y when distributing the negative

review.note: Clare's work has two errors in the same step (12 · 5 written as 72, and −(5 − 9y) written as −5 − 9y). The key gives full credit for naming either one plus the correct solution; Kincaid may want both required.

problems.text: Elena said the equation \(9x+15=3x+15\) has no solutions because \(9x\) is greater than \(3x\). Do you agree with Elena? Explain your reasoning.

answer.sample: No. Subtracting 3x and 15 from both sides gives 6x = 0, so x = 0 is a solution: 9(0) + 15 = 3(0) + 15. 9x is not greater than 3x when x is 0 or negative.
criteria: Shows that x = 0 is a solution, by solving or by substituting

problems.solution: 9x + 15 = 3x + 15 gives 6x = 0, so x = 0. Both sides equal 15 when x = 0.
